findings.title: Index on 400M-row table is not created CONCURRENTLY
findings.explanation: docs/CONVENTIONS.md says indexes on `events` (about 400M rows) must use `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY`. Plain `CREATE INDEX` takes a SHARE lock for the whole build. That blocks all INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on `events` and will likely cause an outage on a table this size. Change the statement to `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY events_project_id_idx ON events (project_id, id DESC);`.

findings.title: Missing `-- migrate:no-transaction` header
findings.explanation: `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` cannot run inside a transaction block. The migration file must start with `-- migrate:no-transaction`, as 004_events.sql does. Without the header, the concurrent build fails once it is added. The header is also required by the repo conventions.

findings.title: Use IF NOT EXISTS and plan for failed concurrent builds
findings.explanation: A failed or cancelled concurrent build leaves an INVALID index behind. A retry then fails because the name already exists. Consider `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS`, and note in the PR that an invalid index must be dropped with `DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY` before retrying. Also mention the expected build time and disk usage for 400M rows.

findings.title: Index design and PR description
findings.explanation: The index matches the query in src/routes/projects.ts, `WHERE project_id = $1 ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 100`. A plain `(project_id, id)` index would also work, because Postgres can scan it backwards. `project_id` is nullable, so consider a partial index with `WHERE project_id IS NOT NULL` if many events have no project. It would also help to include EXPLAIN output in the PR, or to confirm that the sequential scan is really what the query planner uses today.
